title: NEBOSH IGC Exam Preparation & Question Technique
learningObjectives: Understand the IG1 exam format and marking structure
Apply command word technique to write high-scoring exam answers
Structure extended response answers using the NEBOSH marking approach
Practise with example questions and model answers

rows: Open book exam (OBE) — you can use notes and course materials
48 hours from time of opening the question paper
One long-form question with multiple parts
Word-processed response submitted online to NEBOSH
No strict limit but NEBOSH expects approximately 3,000–3,500 words

content.text: The IG1 is open book — this is both an advantage and a trap. Candidates who simply copy text from notes without applying it to the specific scenario will score poorly. NEBOSH wants APPLICATION and ANALYSIS, not regurgitation.
Every exam question begins with a command word. Misunderstanding the command word is the most common reason for poor marks.

rows: Brief description of each point — more than a list, less than a full explanation
Full description with enough detail that the reader understands the concept clearly
Give reasons; justify your answer; show how or why
Give strong reasons and evidence for why something is appropriate
Make observations about; evaluate or assess a given situation

content.text: Question: 'Outline the possible causes of a manual handling injury to a warehouse worker.' Poor answer: 'Heavy loads.' (0–1 marks) Good answer: 'Exceeding personal physical capacity through lifting loads that are too heavy or bulky without mechanical assistance; adopting awkward postures such as bending or twisting while carrying loads in confined racking aisles; failing to rest during sustained manual handling tasks leading to muscle fatigue; inadequate training meaning workers are unaware of correct lifting technique.' (4–5 marks)
For questions worth 10+ marks, structure your answer to maximise coverage:

items: Read the scenario carefully — all answers should refer back to the scenario; generic answers score poorly
Plan before writing — note bullet points for each mark you need to earn
Use sub-headings if the question has multiple parts
Give specific examples from the scenario wherever possible
For 'Explain the consequences' type questions, consider legal, financial, and human consequences
Never repeat the same point in different words — NEBOSH marks each unique point once

rows: Leading cause of fatalities; always examined

content.text: Question: 'A worker has been seriously injured in a forklift truck accident at a distribution warehouse. Outline the immediate actions that should be taken following this accident and the possible legal consequences for the employer.' (10 marks)

Immediate actions: (1) Ensure scene is safe — check for ongoing hazards (fuel spill, unstable vehicle); do not move the casualty unless in immediate danger. (2) Call emergency services immediately — ambulance and, if required, fire service. (3) Administer first aid by a trained first aider while awaiting ambulance. (4) Secure the scene — prevent access to preserve evidence; only emergency services should enter. (5) Notify senior management and HSE department immediately. (6) Begin the internal incident investigation process — appoint an investigator; secure CCTV footage, maintenance records, training records, and witness statements before memories fade. (7) Notify the regulatory authority (HSE, Ministry of Labour, etc.) — notifiable incidents must be reported within defined timeframes. Legal consequences: (8) Regulatory investigation and potential prosecution under health and safety legislation, resulting in unlimited fines and/or imprisonment for individuals. (9) Civil claim for compensation by the injured worker or their family. (10) Reputational damage; loss of business from clients who impose HSE performance requirements on their supply chain. (10/10 marks)

Gulf region NEBOSH candidates: the IG1 exam is globally standardised — you will answer the same questions as candidates in the UK, India, and Australia. However, your answers can reference Gulf-specific context as examples. Mentioning Aramco SEMP, ADNOC standards, or Gulf regulatory frameworks alongside the generic answer demonstrates additional depth and contextual understanding that impresses examiners.
